title: The Theory of Forms in Platonic Metaphysics
text:
Plato's theory posits a distinction between two realms: the physical world perceived through the senses, and the intelligible realm of Forms. This latter domain contains perfect, eternal blueprints or essences—such as Beauty itself or Justice itself—which are the true objects of knowledge.

The Objects of study in this higher reality do not change or decay; they simply *are*. The particulars encountered in daily life are merely imperfect copies or shadows of these eternal Forms. Therefore, genuine understanding requires an intellectual ascent away from sensory experience towards rational contemplation.
